title: Dashlane Review 2026: The Password Manager That Does It All — VPN, Dark Web Monitoring & AI Phishing Protection
content:
*Affiliate disclosure: Some links in this article are affiliate links. We may earn a commission at no extra cost to you. This never affects our ratings or recommendations. [Full disclosure](/disclosure)*

*Last updated: July 20, 2026*

## Quick Answer

**Dashlane** is the Swiss Army knife of password managers in 2026. While competitors like 1Password and Bitwarden focus exclusively on credential storage, Dashlane bundles a full security suite into one subscription: password management, a VPN for WiFi protection, real-time dark web monitoring, and brand-new **AI-powered phishing alerts** that detect scam sites before you type a single character. With plans starting at **$4.99/month** (billed annually) and a Friends & Family plan covering 10 members for just **$7.49/month**, Dashlane delivers exceptional value. It earned a **4.8/5** rating on the Apple App Store (103,000+ reviews) and **4.4/5** on Google Play (241,000+ reviews). The trade-off? Dashlane went web-first in 2024, eliminating desktop apps in favor of a browser extension + web app experience. If you want an all-in-one security tool that covers passwords, VPN, and breach monitoring under one roof, Dashlane is the best option available in 2026.

---

---

## Pros and Cons

### Pros 👍

- **All-in-one security bundle** — Password manager + VPN + dark web monitoring in a single subscription, no need for separate tools
- **AI-powered phishing protection** — Automatically detects and warns about suspicious sites before you log in or enter credentials; catches what email filters miss
- **Best-in-class family plan** — Friends & Family covers 10 members for $7.49/month total, making it the most affordable multi-user option on the market
- **Patented zero-knowledge architecture** — U.S.-patented security model ensures Dashlane cannot see, access, or decrypt your vault data even if compelled by law enforcement
- **Dark Web Monitoring with personalized alerts** — Scans breached databases and dark web marketplaces for your credentials, emails, and financial info, then gives actionable remediation steps
- **Passwordless login** — New users can create accounts without a master password, using biometrics and device-based authentication instead
- **Unlimited sharing** — Share passwords, secure notes, and documents with anyone, even non-Dashlane users, with time-limited access controls
- **1GB encrypted document storage** — Store passports, IDs, insurance cards, and sensitive files in encrypted Secure Notes

### Cons 👎

- **No native desktop apps** — Dashlane discontinued its Windows and macOS desktop applications in 2024; everything now runs through the browser extension and web app, which may frustrate power users
- **Limited offline access** — The web-first architecture means you need an internet connection for most operations, though the extension caches your vault locally
- **VPN not available for family members** — In the Friends & Family plan, only the plan manager gets VPN access; the other 9 members do not receive this feature
- **Passwordless login limited to new users** — The feature is not yet available for existing accounts looking to migrate away from a master password
- **Premium pricing for individuals** — At $4.99/month, it costs slightly more than Bitwarden Premium ($0.83/month) or the free tier of many competitors, though the bundled VPN justifies the price

---

## Who Is Dashlane For?

### ✅ Dashlane Is Ideal For:

- **Everyday users who want simplicity** — One subscription covers passwords, VPN, breach alerts, and secure storage. No need to juggle multiple security subscriptions.
- **Families on a budget** — The Friends & Family plan at $7.49/month for 10 members is an absolute steal — less than a dollar per person.
- **Frequent travelers** — Built-in VPN protects you on hotel, airport, and coffee shop WiFi without a separate NordVPN or ExpressVPN subscription.
- **Small business owners** — Secure sharing with contractors, freelancers, and team members without a full enterprise password management deployment.
- **Anyone burned by data breaches** — Dark Web Monitoring with real-time alerts tells you exactly which accounts are compromised and how to fix them.
- **Mobile-first users** — The iOS and Android apps are polished, with biometric unlock, autofill, and the same full feature set as the web app.

### ❌ Dashlane Is NOT Ideal For:

- **Desktop power users** — If you prefer a native macOS or Windows app with offline mode, 1Password or Bitwarden are better fits.
- **Open-source enthusiasts** — Dashlane's code is proprietary. If transparency and open-source audits are non-negotiable, Bitwarden (fully open-source) is the alternative.
- **Enterprise teams needing SSO** — While Dashlane has business plans with SSO and SCIM, the personal/family plans lack Single Sign-On integration.
- **Users who already have a VPN** — If you're already paying for NordVPN or ExpressVPN, the bundle value diminishes somewhat, though the convenience of a single app is hard to beat.

---

## Detailed Features Breakdown

### 1. Password Management & Autofill

At its core, Dashlane is an excellent password manager. The **AI-powered Autofill** goes beyond simple form detection — it recognizes complex multi-step login flows, two-factor authentication prompts, and even payment forms. Dashlane automatically captures new credentials when you sign up for a service and offers to save them with one click.

The **Password Generator** creates strong, unique passwords with customizable parameters: length (up to 40 characters), character types (letters, numbers, symbols), and ambiguous character exclusion. It can generate passphrases of random words for services that require memorable passwords.

What sets Dashlane apart is the **Password Health dashboard**. Every credential in your vault receives a health score based on strength, uniqueness, and breach status. The dashboard shows you exactly which passwords are weak, reused, or compromised — ranked by urgency — so you know exactly what to change first. In 2026, the dashboard added **"Nudges"**: behavioral suggestions that prompt you to change a weak password the next time you log into that specific site.

**Passkey support** arrived in 2025, and Dashlane now stores and syncs passkeys across all your devices, letting you log into Google, Microsoft, Amazon, and hundreds of other services with biometrics instead of passwords.

### 2. AI-Powered Scam & Phishing Protection (NEW in 2026)

This is Dashlane's headline feature for 2026. The **AI Scam Protection** system runs in your browser extension and analyzes websites in real time before you enter any credentials. Unlike traditional phishing filters that rely on URL blocklists (which are always playing catch-up), Dashlane's AI examines:

- **Domain age and registration patterns** — Sites registered within the last 24 hours with suspicious WHOIS data are flagged
- **Visual similarity to legitimate sites** — The AI compares page structure, logo placement, and form layouts against known-good versions of banking, email, and e-commerce sites
- **SSL certificate anomalies** — Self-signed certificates, mismatched domains, and recently issued certs from suspicious authorities
- **Form destination analysis** — Detects when a login form sends credentials to a different domain than the one displayed in the address bar

When the AI detects a potential scam site, Dashlane displays a full-screen warning with the specific reason for suspicion before you can interact with the page. This is notably more aggressive than the subtle URL bar warnings in Chrome and Firefox, which users routinely ignore.

Dashlane reports that this feature caught **over 1.2 million phishing attempts** in the first half of 2026 across its user base.

### 3. Dark Web Monitoring

Dashlane's Dark Web Monitoring is comprehensive and proactive. It scans:

- **Up to 5 email addresses** — Personal, work, backup emails
- **Credit card numbers and bank accounts** — Financial data breach detection
- **Social Security numbers and national IDs** — Identity theft prevention
- **Usernames and custom terms** — Any personal identifier you want monitored

When a match is found, Dashlane sends an immediate push notification and email with specific details: what was found, on which dark web marketplace or breach database, what data was exposed, and step-by-step remediation instructions. Unlike some competitors that offer dark web monitoring as a premium add-on, Dashlane includes it in both Premium and Friends & Family plans at no extra cost.

The monitoring dashboard shows your overall exposure score and breach history, so you can track your security improvement over time as you remediate compromised accounts.

### 4. VPN for WiFi Protection

The built-in VPN is what truly separates Dashlane from every other password manager on the market. It's a full Hotspot Shield-powered VPN with:

- **Servers in 20+ countries** across North America, Europe, and Asia
- **Unlimited bandwidth** — No data caps, no throttling
- **Automatic activation on unsecured WiFi** — Connects automatically when you join a public network at a coffee shop, airport, or hotel
- **DNS leak protection** — Ensures your ISP and network administrator cannot see which websites you visit
- **Kill switch** — Cuts internet access if the VPN connection drops

The VPN is not as feature-rich as dedicated services like NordVPN or ExpressVPN — it lacks split tunneling, multi-hop connections, and specialty servers for streaming. But for its primary purpose (protecting you on public WiFi), it works reliably. The automatic activation on unsecured networks is particularly valuable: you don't have to remember to turn it on every time you leave home.

One important caveat: the VPN is **only available to the Premium plan holder**, not to the 9 additional members in the Friends & Family plan. Each family member would need their own Premium subscription for VPN access.

### 5. Secure Sharing & Secure Notes

Dashlane's **Secure Sharing** allows you to share passwords, payment methods, and Secure Notes with anyone — even people who don't use Dashlane. Recipients with a Dashlane account receive the shared item directly in their vault. Non-Dashlane users receive a time-limited secure link via email.

Sharing options include:
- **Limited-time access** — Expires after a set duration (1 hour to 30 days)
- **View-only vs. full control** — Some shares are read-only for autofill; others allow the recipient to edit
- **Revocation at any time** — End access to a shared credential instantly

**Secure Notes** provide 1GB of encrypted storage for sensitive documents. You can store:
- Passport scans and driver's licenses
- Insurance cards and medical records
- Tax documents and financial statements
- Software licenses and warranty cards
- Personal identification documents

All Secure Note attachments are encrypted with the same zero-knowledge architecture as your passwords, and they sync across all your devices through the Dashlane web app.

## Plans & Pricing

| Plan | Monthly Price | Annual Price | Key Features |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Premium** | $4.99/mo | $59.88/year | 1 user, unlimited devices, unlimited passwords, dark web monitoring, VPN, phishing alerts, passwordless login, 1GB Secure Notes |
| **Friends & Family** | $7.49/mo | $89.88/year | 10 users, everything in Premium for plan manager, everything except VPN for 9 members, family dashboard |

*Prices shown are USD and may vary by region. All plans are billed annually. Dashlane offers a 14-day free trial on Premium — no credit card required for the trial.*

Dashlane also offers **business plans** starting at approximately **$8/user/month** for Password Management (with SSO, SCIM integration, admin console, and enforceable security policies) and **$4/user/month** for Credential Protection (risk detection, AI phishing protection). Enterprise plans with custom pricing are available for organizations needing volume-optimized licensing and dedicated account management.

### Hidden Costs Analysis

Dashlane is refreshingly transparent about pricing. There are no hidden fees, setup charges, or surprise renewal price hikes. However, a few points worth noting:

- **Annual billing only** — You cannot pay month-to-month. The advertised monthly price requires committing to a full year upfront.
- **No free tier** — Unlike Bitwarden (free unlimited devices) or NordPass (free but limited to one device), Dashlane has no free plan beyond the 14-day trial. You must subscribe to use the service.
- **VPN is single-user** — If you need VPN protection for your entire family, the Friends & Family plan won't cover it; each additional VPN user needs their own Premium subscription.
- **No student, educator, or military discounts** — Unlike competitors that offer discount programs, Dashlane does not.

---

## Buyer's Guide: How to Choose a Password Manager in 2026

Choosing a password manager is one of the most consequential security decisions you'll make. Your password manager holds the keys to your entire digital life — email, banking, social media, work accounts, healthcare records, and everything in between.

**Security architecture should be your first filter.** Look for managers with zero-knowledge encryption, meaning the company cannot access your data even under subpoena. Dashlane, 1Password, NordPass, Bitwarden, and Keeper all meet this standard. Avoid any service that stores a copy of your master password or offers "password recovery" (which means they can decrypt your vault).

**Consider what else you need beyond passwords.** If you travel frequently and use public WiFi, Dashlane's bundled VPN eliminates the need for a separate subscription. If you have a large family, the Friends & Family plan's per-user cost is unmatched. If you're a developer or privacy maximalist, Bitwarden's open-source code and self-hosting option may matter more.

**Platform compatibility matters.** Dashlane's web-first approach means you need an internet connection for full functionality, but it also means consistent performance across Windows, macOS, Linux, iOS, and Android — no platform gets left behind. If you frequently work offline (long flights, remote areas), a manager with robust native desktop apps like 1Password may serve you better.

**Think about your non-technical family members.** The most secure password manager is the one your family actually uses. Dashlane's clean interface, automatic syncing, and mobile-friendly design reduce friction for less tech-savvy users. A password manager that frustrates Grandma will simply not get used — and an unused password manager offers zero security.

---

## Competitor Comparisons

### Dashlane vs 1Password

1Password is Dashlane's closest competitor in terms of reputation and premium positioning. Both cost $4.99/month for individual plans with annual billing. 1Password's strengths are its native desktop apps, offline vault access, and the elegant Watchtower security dashboard. Dashlane counters with the bundled VPN, dark web monitoring, and AI phishing protection — features that would cost $10-15/month more if purchased separately alongside 1Password. If you never use public WiFi and value offline access, go with 1Password. If you want the most comprehensive protection from a single subscription, Dashlane wins.

### Dashlane vs NordPass

NordPass offers a more affordable Premium plan at $1.79/month and bundles nicely with NordVPN if you're already in the Nord ecosystem. NordPass also includes a data breach scanner and password health tool. However, NordPass limits its free plan to one device and the premium plan to 6 devices, while Dashlane offers unlimited devices on all paid plans. Dashlane's AI phishing detection is more advanced than NordPass's email-based breach alerts. For families, Dashlane's 10-member plan at $7.49/month dramatically undercuts NordPass Family at $3.69/month for 6 users.

### Dashlane vs Bitwarden

Bitwarden is the open-source champion with a remarkably generous free tier (unlimited devices, unlimited passwords) and a Premium plan at just $0.83/month. It supports self-hosting, has been audited by Cure53, and attracts developers and privacy enthusiasts. The trade-off is feature breadth: Bitwarden lacks a built-in VPN, has no AI phishing detection, and its interface is functional but not as polished as Dashlane's. Bitwarden's Family plan ($3.33/month for 6 users) is cheaper per user than Dashlane, but Dashlane covers 10 users and adds VPN + dark web monitoring. If budget and open-source matter most, Bitwarden is unbeatable. If you want maximum protection with minimal subscriptions, go Dashlane.

### Dashlane vs Keeper

Keeper matches Dashlane on price ($4.99/month for Unlimited) but charges extra for add-ons: BreachWatch dark web monitoring costs $2.92/month more, and KeeperChat secure messaging is separate. Keeper does offer native desktop apps and a wider range of enterprise compliance certifications (FedRAMP, SOC 2, ISO 27001). For individual and family users, Dashlane's all-inclusive pricing is significantly better value. For organizations handling classified or highly regulated data, Keeper's compliance certifications make it the more appropriate choice.

### Dashlane vs LastPass

LastPass was once the market leader, but catastrophic data breaches in 2022 (source code theft, customer vault data exfiltration) severely damaged its reputation. In 2026, LastPass struggles with user trust despite security improvements and a new management team. LastPass offers a robust free tier (unlimited passwords, one device type) that Dashlane lacks. However, the trust deficit is substantial. After the breaches, security researchers and cybersecurity journalists broadly recommended migrating away from LastPass. For anyone evaluating these two options side by side in 2026, the choice is clear: Dashlane's track record, architecture, and feature set make it the superior option.

---

## Real-World Performance & User Feedback

Dashlane's reputation is backed by an impressive volume of user ratings across platforms:

- **Apple App Store: 4.8/5** — 103,789 ratings. Users consistently praise the autofill reliability, clean interface, and biometric unlock on iOS. Top review themes: "seamless integration," "worth every penny," "finally makes password management effortless."
- **Google Play: 4.4/5** — 241,113 ratings, 5,000,000+ installs. Android users appreciate the cross-device sync and the autofill accessibility service that works across browsers and apps. Common praise: "the best password manager I've tried," "dark web monitoring gives peace of mind."
- **G2: 4.5/5** — Approximately 626 reviews. G2 named Dashlane a Password Manager and Single Sign-On Leader in 2026 based on user satisfaction scores.
- **Awards:** PC Mag "Editors' Choice" for password managers multiple years running, PCWorld "Best Password Manager," Webby Award "People's Voice" winner.

Common themes in critical reviews: frustration with the removal of desktop apps (before 2024), occasional autofill failures on uncommon login forms (e.g., government websites with non-standard authentication flows), and the VPN's limited server count compared to dedicated services. Support response times receive mixed feedback: live chat is generally responsive, but complex technical issues sometimes require escalation and multi-day resolution.

---

## Tips for Getting the Most Out of Dashlane

1. **Install the extension on every browser you use** — Dashlane works best when it's everywhere. Install it on Chrome, Firefox, Edge, and Safari to ensure you never type a password manually.

2. **Run the Password Health audit every month** — Set a calendar reminder. The dashboard will show you exactly which passwords need changing, prioritized by risk level. Fix the "compromised" ones first.

3. **Enable the VPN's auto-connect on unsecured WiFi** — This is a toggle in settings. Once enabled, you'll never accidentally browse on public WiFi without protection. The peace of mind alone is worth the subscription.

4. **Add all your email addresses to Dark Web Monitoring** — Most people have 2-4 email addresses (personal, work, backup, old accounts). Monitor all of them; breaches on your "junk" email are just as dangerous if they contain reused passwords.

5. **Use passkeys wherever possible** — For services that support passkeys (Google, Microsoft, Amazon, eBay, PayPal, Adobe, and increasingly more), enable them. Passkeys are phishing-resistant and cannot be stolen in database breaches.

6. **Create a Secure Note for your digital estate** — Store emergency contacts, insurance policies, financial account numbers, and critical documents in an encrypted note. Share it with a trusted family member with limited-time access.

7. **Use the Friends & Family plan strategically** — Even if you don't have 10 household members, consider splitting the subscription with close friends or extended family. At $0.75/person/month, it's the best value in password management.

---

## FAQ

### Is Dashlane safe?

Yes. Dashlane uses a U.S.-patented zero-knowledge security architecture with AES-256 encryption. Your master password is never stored on Dashlane's servers, and the company cannot access or decrypt your vault data. All encryption and decryption happens locally on your device. Dashlane has undergone independent security audits and maintains a bug bounty program with HackerOne. No breach of Dashlane's encrypted vault data has ever occurred.

### What happens if I forget my master password?

Dashlane cannot recover your master password because they don't store it. If you forget it, you can use the account recovery feature (if you set it up beforehand) which uses biometric verification on a trusted mobile device. Without recovery set up, forgetting your master password means losing access to your vault permanently — this is a security feature, not a flaw. The new passwordless login (available for new accounts created in 2026) eliminates this risk by using device-based biometric authentication instead of a master password.

### Does Dashlane offer a free plan?

No. Dashlane discontinued its free plan and now only offers paid subscriptions: Premium ($4.99/month) and Friends & Family ($7.49/month). They offer a 14-day free trial with no credit card required so you can test the full Premium experience before committing.

### Does the Dashlane VPN work with Netflix and streaming?

Dashlane's VPN is designed for WiFi security and privacy protection, not for streaming. It uses a limited number of server locations and IP addresses that streaming services readily identify and block. If you need a VPN specifically for Netflix, Hulu, BBC iPlayer, or other geo-restricted content, a dedicated streaming VPN like NordVPN, ExpressVPN, or Surfshark is necessary. Dashlane's VPN should be viewed as a privacy tool, not a streaming tool.

### Can I use Dashlane offline?

Limited offline access is available. The browser extension caches your vault data locally, so you can autofill passwords and access stored items without an internet connection. However, syncing changes across devices, accessing the web app dashboard, and receiving dark web alerts all require connectivity. Dashlane is not designed for extended offline use.

### What platforms and browsers does Dashlane support?

Dashlane works on iOS, Android, macOS, Windows, and Linux through its browser extension and web app. Supported browsers include Chrome, Firefox, Edge, Safari, and Brave. The native Windows and macOS desktop apps were discontinued in 2024; all functionality now runs through the browser extension and web app at app.dashlane.com.

### How does Dashlane compare to iCloud Keychain?

iCloud Keychain is Apple's free built-in password manager. It works well within the Apple ecosystem (Safari, iPhone, iPad, Mac) but is essentially unusable outside it. Dashlane offers platform-agnostic syncing across iOS, Android, Windows, Mac, and Linux, plus features iCloud Keychain lacks: dark web monitoring, VPN, phishing protection, secure sharing with non-Apple users, and a password health dashboard. If everyone you share passwords with uses Apple devices exclusively and you don't need the extra security features, iCloud Keychain may suffice. For everyone else, Dashlane is the upgrade.

### Does Dashlane support biometric login?

Yes. Dashlane supports fingerprint unlock (Touch ID on iOS and macOS, fingerprint sensors on Android and Windows Hello), facial recognition (Face ID on iOS), and PIN unlock on mobile. Biometric authentication is processed locally on your device and never transmitted to Dashlane's servers.

### Can I import passwords from another password manager?

Yes. Dashlane supports importing from over 20 password managers and browsers, including 1Password, LastPass, Bitwarden, NordPass, Keeper, Chrome, Firefox, Safari, and CSV files. The import process takes 2-3 minutes: export your data from the old manager as a CSV file, upload it to Dashlane's import tool, and all your credentials, secure notes, and payment methods appear in your new vault.

### Is Dashlane's VPN a real VPN or just a proxy?

Dashlane's VPN is a full VPN powered by Hotspot Shield's infrastructure, providing encrypted tunneling for all internet traffic from your device. It is not a proxy, smart DNS, or browser-only extension. The encrypted tunnel protects your entire connection — websites, apps, and background services — not just your browser traffic.

### How does Dashlane's Friends & Family plan work?

The Friends & Family plan includes 1 plan manager (who pays the subscription and has access to all Premium features including VPN) plus 9 additional members. Plan members get unlimited passwords, dark web monitoring, secure sharing, and all Premium features except VPN. The plan manager can view member status and manage invitations from a dashboard but cannot see members' stored passwords or vault contents (zero-knowledge privacy applies to every account individually). Members can be added, removed, and replaced at any time.

---

## Conclusion

Dashlane is the most complete personal security package you can buy with a single subscription in 2026. It combines a top-tier password manager, VPN, dark web monitoring, and AI-driven phishing protection into one polished product that works across every device and platform you own.

The removal of native desktop apps in 2024 was controversial, and power users who prefer a dedicated application may still prefer 1Password or Bitwarden. But for the vast majority of people — families, professionals, frequent travelers, and anyone who wants to stop worrying about online security — Dashlane's all-in-one approach is the smartest choice.

The Friends & Family plan is genuinely the best value in the password management space. At $7.49/month for 10 people, you're paying less than Netflix for comprehensive digital security for your entire household. Add the 14-day free trial with no credit card required, and there's zero risk in giving Dashlane a try.

If you want a password manager that does more than just manage passwords — one that actively protects you from phishing, monitors the dark web for your stolen data, and keeps you safe on public WiFi — Dashlane is the best option available today.
